intent: Record that Balatro's die replaces its ONE pip with the joker as a settled fact rather than an open assumption. The player owns the game and confirmed the mapping, so the data and the docs should stop hedging on it.
scope: kcd2_dice_solver/src/data/dice.ts - the comment on the Balatro entry
kcd2_dice_solver/README.md - the 'what the numbers are not' bullet
Non-goal: any behaviour change. wildcardFaces was already [1]; only the wording around it moves.
changes: The UNVERIFIED caveat on the joker's face is replaced with the confirmation and its consequence: the joker sits where the 1 used to be, so the die has no plain single pip, which is also why holding it alone counts as a 1.
The README no longer calls the mapping unverified. Uniform side weights remain flagged as the one real assumption, since no source publishes them.

verification.evidence: 222 tests pass, unchanged - this commit touches a comment and a paragraph, not code paths.
No type errors, no lint findings.

risks: The claim now rests on the player's confirmation rather than a citable source; no wiki page states which pip the joker replaces. If it is ever contradicted in-game, dice.ts's wildcardFaces and this wording move together.
The die's side weights are still assumed uniform. That assumption is unchanged and still marked in both the data and the README.
rollback: git revert the commit; the wording returns to UNVERIFIED and no behaviour changes either way.
After rollback, confirm dice.ts still has wildcardFaces: [1] for balatro - the mapping itself was never in doubt in the code, only in the prose.
